sentences.text: Revenue grew from $4.86 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F10], a 12.8% compound annual rate [F198].
Revenue rose 89.1% to $16.1 billion in FY2021 [D241][F6] and then fell 24.3% in FY2022 [D292], so the window is cyclical rather than steady compounding.
Net product sales supplied 77.1pp of that growth [D495], mostly REGEN-COV U.S. sales of $5.83 billion [S48] under a September 2021 U.S. government supply agreement [P39].
REGEN-COV U.S. sales were $0 in FY2022 [S49]; the FY2021 10-K says an FDA revision left REGEN-COV no longer authorized for use [P43].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits was the largest positive driver, adding 9.3pp to FY2025 growth [D592] and reaching $5.24 billion [S52].
The filing ties that rise to higher Dupixent sales, with the profit share up 33.6% [D591] [P9].
EYLEA U.S. sales fell 42.4% [D577], subtracting 14.2pp [D578], on lower volumes, competitive pressure and lower net prices [P10].
Operating income fell 10.3% [D441] on 1.0% revenue growth [D440], while operating costs rose 5.4% [D457], so profit lagged revenue.
Diluted EPS rose 8.2% [D444] against 2.1% net income growth [D442], helped by a 5.6% lower diluted share count [D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% [F30] equals the window low [D749] and sits 9.7pp below the 34.6% window median [D751] [F30].
The biopharma peer median operating margin is 34.0% [D773], and the company ranks at the 33rd percentile [D772] among three peers [D773].
SG&A fell 8.6% [D456], adding 2.0pp [D466] on lower charitable contributions [P5]; R&D, up 14.0% [D455], cost 4.7pp [D465].
The FY2022 fall of 16.7pp [D305] came mainly from R&D at 11.4pp [D318] and SG&A at 6.0pp [D319], where headcount and Libtayo costs rose [P34].
Net margin of 31.4% [F50] ran 6.5pp above operating margin [F30] [F50], as other income reached $1.65 billion [X117] against $789 million [X116].
Free cash flow was 0.91x net income [D429], against a 0.88x window median [D763] and a 1.11x peer median [D783].
The free cash flow margin of 28.4% [D425] is above its 26.4% window median [D757], with operating cash flow of $4.98 billion [F80].
Capex of $898 million [F90] was 6.3% of revenue [D424] and 1.65x D&A [D430], up 18.9% [D447]; the cited filings do not explain that rise.
The FY2020 low of 0.57x [D761] followed a $1.36 billion receivables build, partly from extended EYLEA payment terms [P51].
Net cash of $16.9 billion [D434] equals 117.7% of revenue [D435], ranking 100th percentile among eight peers [D780] against a -50.7% median [D781].
Debt of $1.99 billion [F187] dates from $1.98 billion of FY2020 issuance [X148], tied to a bridge loan facility and senior notes [P53].
Buybacks of $3.44 billion [X137] and dividends of $370 million [X140] took 93.3% of free cash flow [D437], and diluted shares fell 5.6% [D459].
Capital returns now absorb nearly all free cash flow, so per-share growth leans more on buybacks than on profit growth.
Operating margin fell four years in a row, 30.7pp in total [R1], from 55.7% in FY2021 [D750] to 24.9% in FY2025 [F30].
EYLEA U.S. sales fell 42.4% in FY2025 [D577], and combined EYLEA HD and EYLEA sales dropped to $4.38 billion from $5.97 billion [S46] [S45].
The 42.4% EYLEA U.S. decline [D577] is attributed to competition, compounded bevacizumab, the move to EYLEA HD and lower prices [P10].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts [R2], so growth across that pair mixes presentations and is not used here.
Operating margin below its FY2025 low of 24.9% [D749] would confirm the decline, while a return toward the 34.6% median [D751] would reverse it; both appear in the FY2026 10-K.
Combined EYLEA HD and EYLEA U.S. sales below $4.38 billion [S46] would confirm the erosion, while growth above $5.97 billion [S45] would reverse it; both appear in the FY2026 10-K.
The Sanofi antibody profit share, $5.24 billion in FY2025 [S52], is the main growth driver, so a fall below the FY2024 level of $3.92 billion [S51] would reverse that growth in the FY2026 10-K.
